nmap -sV -p PORT ASSIGNED_HOST
ncat ASSIGNED_HOST PORT

kali-95.first_action: Use Node's Buffer API for a known byte representation and verify both decoded bytes and round-trip encoding before adapting a JavaScript helper.
kali-95.expected: Explicit binary/text conversion without accidental Unicode assumptions.
kali-95.fallback: Buffer decoding may accept malformed input differently from a strict parser; validate the source alphabet and length first.

kali-96.first_action: Confirm the script resembles supported Obfuscator.io output; run the installed local deobfuscator on a copy and inspect recovered strings/control flow.
kali-96.expected: Readable candidate expressions that can be compared with the original.
kali-96.fallback: Unsupported transforms need manual analysis or js-beautify; do not upload challenge code to the advertised service.

kali-97.first_action: Open a local Obsidian vault and keep one note per question with evidence paths, observations and linked hypotheses.
kali-97.expected: Notes distinguish observed facts, candidate explanations and the next check.
kali-97.fallback: If plugins or startup fail, use the existing Markdown editor; plain local notes are sufficient and do not require synchronization.

kali-98.first_action: Choose the Office parser by artifact: oleid for triage, olevba for VBA, rtfobj/oleobj for embedded objects, and msodde when DDE is the clue.
kali-98.expected: Extracted code or objects tied to their document streams.
kali-98.fallback: Never enable macros to inspect them; unsupported containers need archive/object inspection and decoded content still requires analysis.

kali-99.first_action: For a legacy 32-bit Windows checker, open it in the existing OllyDbg setup and break at the identified check before testing a known input.
kali-99.expected: Registers and memory show the comparison and branch.
kali-99.fallback: The recorded Wine build may not run reliably; use x32dbg where available or continue static inspection.

kali-100.first_action: If clues point to OpenStego, use its Extract Data workflow on the image with the supplied/clue-derived password and a fresh output directory.
kali-100.expected: A recovered embedded payload validated by its content.
kali-100.fallback: An incorrect password or different embedding scheme can look like no data; use carrier-specific evidence rather than treating OpenStego as a universal LSB decoder.

kali-101.first_action: Confirm a stable valid/invalid padding distinction with a baseline and negative control on the assigned CBC endpoint; match block size and transport encoding before using the attacker.
kali-101.expected: Oracle responses are reproducible enough for a candidate plaintext/decryption result to be checked.
kali-101.fallback: Rate limits, generic errors or inconsistent responses invalidate the oracle; resolve the signal before spending requests.

kali-102.first_action: In GP, use a small known integer to confirm factorization and modular-arithmetic conventions, then apply the operation justified by the challenge.
kali-102.expected: Factors or modular results that satisfy the original equation.
kali-102.fallback: Large inputs may be infeasible; use structural clues rather than assuming generic factorization is cheap.

kali-103.first_action: Open the local PayloadsAllTheThings section for the suspected vulnerability and compare its prerequisites with a captured request before selecting one test.
kali-103.expected: A single input change and negative control support or reject the hypothesis.
kali-103.fallback: Syntax examples may depend on a different parser/version; adapt from actual errors and do not treat linked tools as automatically approved.

kali-104.first_action: Use the preconfigured PEDA session in GDB, stop at the known check and inspect its register, stack and disassembly context.
kali-104.expected: State at the breakpoint explains how a known input is handled.
kali-104.fallback: If plugin initialization conflicts, use plain GDB or one frontend; do not stack PEDA with GEF/pwndbg.

kali-105.first_action: Open the PDF in peepdf-3 and inspect its object graph, suspicious references and decoded streams relevant to the clue.
kali-105.expected: A specific object/stream explains embedded code or unusual document behavior.
kali-105.fallback: Optional JavaScript features may be unavailable; extract/inspect the stream with qpdf or pdf-parser rather than executing it.

kali-106.first_action: Inspect PST/OST metadata, then export relevant messages and attachments to a separate directory using the installed libpff tools.
kali-106.expected: Message headers, timestamps and attachment files linked to the mailbox.
kali-106.fallback: Check supported mailbox variant and local pffexport options; corruption or partial stores may limit recovery.

kali-107.first_action: Parse only the relevant artifact set into a new Plaso storage file; inspect its metadata with pinfo and export the question's interval with psort.
kali-107.expected: A timeline retaining parser/source provenance and normalized timestamp interpretation.
kali-107.fallback: Whole-image parsing may waste time; narrow inputs and verify time zones and timestamp semantics before correlating events.

kali-108.first_action: Inspect PNG chunks and integrity before attempting pixel-bit analysis. Record text chunks, unexpected trailing data and any CRC/truncation errors.
kali-108.expected: Structural findings distinguish format damage from a steganography lead.
kali-108.fallback: Check local version options and confirm with another PNG reader; valid structure does not exclude LSB content.

kali-109.first_action: Start the existing pwndbg configuration alone, stop at a known input-check location and inspect registers, stack and pointed-to memory.
kali-109.expected: Runtime operands tied to the supplied input and instruction.
kali-109.fallback: Resolve debugger/plugin compatibility or fall back to plain GDB; do not combine competing .gdbinit frontends.

kali-110.first_action: Identify the PYC version and try pycdc; compare incomplete or questionable reconstruction with pycdas disassembly.
kali-110.expected: Candidate Python logic supported by bytecode instructions.
kali-110.fallback: Unsupported opcodes can make output partial or wrong; select another decompiler only if it supports that bytecode version.

kali-111.first_action: Extract a copied PyInstaller bundle with pyinstxtractor-ng, record the reported Python version and identify the application PYC among bundled dependencies.
kali-111.expected: Bytecode and resources available for static inspection.
kali-111.fallback: Extraction is not decompilation; use a version-compatible decompiler and inspect the wrapper if the bundle format is unsupported.

kali-112.first_action: Select pypykatz's offline minidump parser for an explicitly supplied Windows authentication dump and inspect only relevant records locally.
kali-112.expected: Supported authentication structures with source context.
kali-112.fallback: Build/dump incompatibility is not proof of absent data; keep recovered values private and avoid replacing offline analysis with live acquisition.

kali-113.first_action: Use Python 2.7 only for a reviewed legacy script; verify byte-string, integer-division and struct assumptions with a known sample before challenge input.
kali-113.expected: The legacy interpreter reproduces the expected parser behavior.
kali-113.fallback: Port a small understood operation to Python 3 when practical; a Python 2 script's imports may still be missing offline.

kali-114.first_action: Check whether uv already has Python 3.11 available and select it for a script that requires that version; confirm the executable actually used.
kali-114.expected: Interpreter output identifies Python 3.11 in the intended environment.
kali-114.fallback: The workbook has no installation evidence; if unavailable offline, use a compatible prepared interpreter or document the requirement.

kali-115.first_action: Inspect virtual-disk format and backing files before converting a copy to raw with enough free output space.
kali-115.expected: Correct source format/backing chain and a raw image suitable for filesystem tools.
kali-115.fallback: Missing backing files make dependent images incomplete; do not modify an image in use or mistake conversion for recovery.

kali-116.first_action: Open the binary in radare2, inspect information/strings and analyze only enough functions to locate the input check; disassemble that routine.
kali-116.expected: Function addresses and references explain the comparison.
kali-116.fallback: Broad analysis can be costly or misleading; use targeted navigation or Ghidra, and do not assume Cutter/Rizin commands are identical.

kali-117.first_action: Confirm evidence for a supported RAT family, then select the matching rat-king-parser family workflow on a copied sample.
kali-117.expected: Extracted configuration fields that agree with the sample's code or strings.
kali-117.fallback: Variant coverage is finite; empty output does not prove no configuration, so inspect the storage/decryption routine manually.

kali-118.first_action: Identify the offline registry hive type and select the relevant installed RegRipper 3 plugin; retain plugin name and source hive with its output.
kali-118.expected: Keys, values and available timestamps relevant to the question.
kali-118.fallback: Transaction logs are not replayed automatically; note missing recent state and use another approved parser if replay is required.

kali-119.first_action: Search a relevant directory for a literal clue with line numbers; include hidden files only when the evidence warrants it.
kali-119.expected: Matches with paths and line context for focused inspection.
kali-119.fallback: Ignored/hidden/binary files are normally skipped; deliberately adjust scope rather than assuming no match means absence.

kali-120.first_action: Locate the installed rockyou wordlist and check whether it is compressed; make a separate decompressed copy if needed and pass its real path to one offline cracking attempt.
kali-120.expected: A readable local candidate dictionary used by the selected cracking tool.
kali-120.fallback: A wordlist is not a cracking engine and may omit the answer; use challenge clues to narrow candidates rather than repeatedly rerunning it.

kali-121.first_action: Search the copied native binary for the small gadget class required by an already identified exploitation primitive; inspect candidate instructions in disassembly.
kali-121.expected: Usable instruction sequences with file-relative/runtime-address assumptions recorded.
kali-121.fallback: A gadget address needs the correct load base and safe side effects; its existence alone does not establish an exploit.

kali-122.first_action: Identify whether the supplied recording is an rtptools dump or a PCAP; use the matching rtptools inspection/replay workflow only for its supported RTP dump format.
kali-122.expected: RTP headers, sequence numbers and timing can be examined or replayed in an isolated endpoint.
kali-122.fallback: Replay is not audio decoding; for PCAP use Wireshark RTP analysis and decode the payload with the correct codec.

kali-123.first_action: Inspect the installed Rust toolchain and a reviewed project's Cargo manifest; build using locally available dependencies when a Rust utility is required.
kali-123.expected: A compiled program matching the required edition/toolchain.
kali-123.fallback: Missing crates block offline builds; use an existing executable or approved equivalent rather than introducing a new dependency stack.

kali-124.first_action: Use RustScan only when port discovery is needed for the assigned host; choose conservative batch/timeout settings, then verify selected ports with Nmap service detection.
kali-124.expected: A small list of reachable TCP ports with independently checked services.
kali-124.fallback: High concurrency can lose results or overload the environment; use direct Nmap for explicit ports or unclear results.

kali-125.first_action: Confirm SageMath availability, reproduce a small known finite-field/group example, then formulate the exact modular equation or discrete-log problem from challenge parameters.
kali-125.expected: A candidate solution verified by substitution or exponentiation in the original group.
kali-125.fallback: Missing installation or a large hard group blocks the method; use structural weaknesses and check group order rather than assuming arbitrary logs are easy.

kali-126.first_action: Locate the installed SecLists data directory and select a short list suited to paths, usernames or the specific content-discovery task.
kali-126.expected: A deliberate wordlist path and scope for the chosen tool.
kali-126.fallback: The workbook's executable-like location is not proof of the data directory; inspect installed files and avoid using the largest list by default.

kali-127.first_action: Connect standard input/output to the assigned plaintext TCP endpoint with socat and send one protocol-appropriate line.
kali-127.expected: A banner or response confirms stream behavior.
kali-127.fallback: Check address syntax and whether TLS is required; prefer Ncat for a simple interaction rather than adding unnecessary bridges/listeners.

kali-128.first_action: Open audio in Sonic Visualiser, add a spectrogram layer and align separate panes/channels to measure tone frequencies or pulse timing.
kali-128.expected: Measurable time/frequency intervals supporting a decoder or symbol mapping.
kali-128.fallback: Adjust FFT/window settings and channel selection; use Audacity for basic inspection when measurement detail is unnecessary.

kali-129.first_action: Confirm whether the installed executable is SoX_ng and inspect its supported effects; create a spectrogram or channel derivative only after checking input rate/channels.
kali-129.expected: A repeatable derived audio view with explicit processing settings.
kali-129.fallback: Exact options may differ from legacy SoX; use Audacity or FFmpeg when the local build cannot perform the intended operation.

kali-130.first_action: Open the copied SQLCipher database, supply the known key interactively and set the required compatibility/KDF parameters before the first query.
kali-130.expected: A readable schema and rows from the encrypted database.
kali-130.fallback: Wrong compatibility settings can resemble a wrong key; verify the producer's SQLCipher version rather than treating this CLI as a password cracker.

kali-131.first_action: Open the copied SQLite database read-only with its sidecars; inspect tables/schema, then query only the relevant rows and timestamp fields.
kali-131.expected: Records whose table, column and time encoding can be explained.
kali-131.fallback: Preserve WAL files and check application-specific timestamp units; missing rows may require deleted-record analysis.

kali-132.first_action: Save a reproducible captured HTTP request and identify the suspected parameter; run the low-risk single-thread sqlmap check against that parameter only.
kali-132.expected: Injection evidence tied to a specific input and reproducible response distinction.
kali-132.fallback: Refresh authentication and verify baseline/negative controls; do not raise risk or enumerate data to compensate for an unstable request.

kali-133.first_action: Inspect the actual installed executable/package before decoding: the workbook labels sstv a decoder but records PySSTV, which is an encoder.
kali-133.expected: A confirmed identity shows whether an approved decoder is actually available.
kali-133.fallback: Do not assume colaclanth/sstv is installed from the row name. If only PySSTV exists, inspect audio visually and record the decoding gap.

kali-134.first_action: Inspect supported carrier information, then extract with the supplied or clue-derived passphrase into a new file.
kali-134.expected: A steghide payload whose recovered bytes validate.
kali-134.fallback: PNG is not a supported steghide carrier; wrong passphrase or a different embedding scheme needs a new hypothesis.

kali-135.first_action: For a likely steghide carrier, run a focused wordlist attempt to a new output; use seed detection only with its documented limits.
kali-135.expected: A validated payload and, where found, its matching password candidate.
kali-135.fallback: Seed mode detects structure; passwordless recovery requires unencrypted data. A wrong carrier or exhausted list needs evidence, not claims of decryption.

kali-136.first_action: Preserve the original text's trailing spaces/tabs and use stegsnow's decode mode, adding a supplied password only if the clue requires it.
kali-136.expected: Decoded bytes from the untouched whitespace carrier.
kali-136.fallback: Copy/paste or editor cleanup can destroy the payload; return to the original file and check whether compression/password settings apply.

kali-137.first_action: Open the original image in a working StegSolve GUI and inspect the clue's channel/bit planes; use Data Extract only after choosing a concrete order/plane hypothesis.
kali-137.expected: A visible pattern or extracted byte sequence that can be reproduced.
kali-137.fallback: The recorded launch failed headlessly and the reference fork may differ; use zsteg or derived channel views if the GUI is unavailable.

kali-138.first_action: In an isolated environment, trace the challenge binary's relevant file/process syscalls with a known input and save the trace separately.
kali-138.expected: Paths, failures or child-process activity explain missing inputs or hidden dependencies.
kali-138.fallback: Linux execution is required; for static triage or incompatible binaries, inspect strings/disassembly instead.

kali-139.first_action: Query a challenge-supplied public domain with Subfinder while retaining source provenance, then corroborate candidate names in their cited public sources.
kali-139.expected: Hostname candidates with source information and observation time.
kali-139.fallback: Public indexes can be stale and private domains may have no entries; absence is not evidence that no host exists.

kali-140.first_action: Open the local source/notes directory in Sublime Text and use project search for an identified symbol or clue; inspect surrounding code before editing a copy.
kali-140.expected: Relevant definitions and call sites with file context.
kali-140.fallback: Use ripgrep for large trees or unsupported encodings; an editor search does not parse binary formats.

kali-141.first_action: List archive members first, inspect paths and sizes, then extract the relevant members into a fresh directory.
kali-141.expected: Expected files recovered without overwriting the source tree.
kali-141.fallback: Check compression and missing multipart data; treat absolute/traversal paths and symlink members carefully before extraction.

kali-142.first_action: Read a supplied capture with a narrow host/port/protocol filter and a bounded packet count before escalating to stream reconstruction.
kali-142.expected: Packet summaries identify relevant peers and protocols.
kali-142.fallback: tcpdump filters differ from Wireshark display filters; use Wireshark/TShark when payload reassembly or protocol fields are needed.

kali-143.first_action: Use TestDisk's file-list/copy workflow on an image when filesystem metadata survives; use PhotoRec carving only when metadata recovery cannot locate the content.
kali-143.expected: Recovered files in a separate destination, with names/paths where metadata permits.
kali-143.fallback: Carving loses original names and fragmented files may fail; validate file content and never recover into the source image/device.

kali-144.first_action: List supported archive contents with the accompanying lsar tool, then extract selected content with unar to a new directory using local options.
kali-144.expected: Member metadata and extracted files for the next format-specific tool.
kali-144.fallback: Check multipart volumes, passwords and format support; use 7-Zip for another local archive view.

kali-145.first_action: Identify the PYC bytecode version before using uncompyle6 and compare important conditions with disassembly.
kali-145.expected: Reconstructed older Python source supported by the bytecode.
kali-145.fallback: Its documented support reaches Python 3.8 bytecode; running it under a newer interpreter does not add newer opcode support.

kali-146.first_action: Match the supplied PYC to unpyc37-3.10's documented version coverage, then use its installed entry point for an alternate decompilation view.
kali-146.expected: Partial or complete candidate source with version limits explicitly recorded.
kali-146.fallback: Support declines across 3.7–3.10; use pycdas or another version-compatible view rather than trusting incomplete output.

kali-147.first_action: List the RAR archive, test its integrity and extract needed members into a new directory with all supplied volumes present.
kali-147.expected: Member names and integrity results before recovery.
kali-147.fallback: Missing volumes or a password are different from corruption; resolve those inputs before repeatedly extracting.

kali-148.first_action: List ZIP members and test the archive before extracting selected entries to a fresh directory.
kali-148.expected: Names, sizes and integrity diagnostics that select the useful file.
kali-148.fallback: Check encryption and unsupported ZIP features; use 7-Zip for another parser and do not ignore failed CRC checks.

kali-149.first_action: Test a suspected UPX executable, then unpack to a new file and identify/analyze that output statically.
kali-149.expected: A recognized packed file and a separate unpacked executable.
kali-149.fallback: Modified packers can defeat normal unpacking; inspect code/sections rather than claiming every UPX-like file is handled.

kali-150.first_action: Open the local analysis folder in VS Code with untrusted-workspace restrictions appropriate to unknown code; search the input handling and edit only reviewed scripts.
kali-150.expected: Definitions, call sites and the intended interpreter/build context are visible.
kali-150.fallback: Do not accept automatic tasks/extensions from an unknown repository; use plain text search when code execution is unnecessary.

kali-151.first_action: For a supported legacy Windows memory image, obtain profile suggestions and corroborate the OS/build before running process or network plugins with that profile.
kali-151.expected: Consistent legacy memory structures and process records.
kali-151.fallback: Wrong profiles produce misleading output; use matching evidence and Volatility 3 for a supported newer image rather than mixing command syntax.

kali-152.first_action: Select one Volatility 2 community plugin for the artifact missing from core coverage; read its dependencies and load it with the matching profile.
kali-152.expected: The plugin appears in help and returns records consistent with known core-plugin findings.
kali-152.fallback: Check plugin API/Python compatibility; a directory of community plugins is not blanket proof that every plugin works.

kali-153.first_action: Match the memory image's exact Linux/macOS build to an available Volatility 2 profile and verify recognized core structures before using artifact plugins.
kali-153.expected: A profile whose output agrees with independent OS/kernel evidence.
kali-153.fallback: A similarly named kernel is insufficient; if no exact profile exists, report the gap or use the compatible Volatility 3 symbol route.

kali-154.first_action: Choose the specific Volatility 3 community plugin needed, inspect its release requirements and load it from an explicit plugin directory.
kali-154.expected: The plugin is discoverable and produces plausible records with the image's matching symbols.
kali-154.fallback: Upstream warns of incompatibility with current Volatility 3; use a core plugin or report unsupported behavior instead of assuming presence means readiness.

kali-155.first_action: Select the built C/C++ executable and matching GDB/debug symbols in VS Code's C/C++ debug configuration, then stop at a known source line in a reviewed local program.
kali-155.expected: Source breakpoints correspond to actual instructions and variables.
kali-155.fallback: Rebuild with debug information and check working directory/architecture; use standalone GDB if editor integration obscures the failure.

kali-156.first_action: Select the intended Python environment through the VS Code Python extension and confirm the displayed interpreter matches a terminal version check before debugging a reviewed script.
kali-156.expected: Imports and breakpoints use the same interpreter as the command-line workflow.
kali-156.fallback: If imports differ, fix interpreter selection rather than installing duplicates globally; verify extension availability offline.

kali-157.first_action: Compile a small meaningful YARA rule and scan a local sample plus a near-miss control; inspect matched strings and offsets.
kali-157.expected: A pattern match that distinguishes the intended bytes from the control.
kali-157.fallback: A hit is not a malware verdict; refine overly broad strings and validate syntax/conditions before scanning a large corpus.

kali-158.first_action: Use yara-python only when an existing Python workflow needs structured matches; compile the same rule used by the CLI and compare results on the same sample/control.
kali-158.expected: Python match data agrees with the CLI for the selected rule and files.
kali-158.fallback: Check binding/library version compatibility; use the YARA CLI directly when no structured integration is needed.

kali-159.first_action: Package only the intended harmless files into a new ZIP, then list/test it and compare member names before transferring or keeping it as a fixture.
kali-159.expected: An archive with the selected files and unchanged originals.
kali-159.fallback: Check relative paths and accidental sensitive files; use an existing archive tool rather than a new packaging script.

kali-160.first_action: Test the Zstandard stream and decompress to a separate destination using the installed CLI.
kali-160.expected: Integrity diagnostics and a decoded payload to identify.
kali-160.fallback: A dictionary-compressed frame needs its matching dictionary; confirm framing and missing inputs before blaming the decoder.

kali-161.first_action: Import an already supported capture-derived dataset into Zui and query connections/protocol records by the relevant endpoint or time window.
kali-161.expected: A small set of records that can be traced to packets or source logs.
kali-161.fallback: Verify the installed version and PCAP-import dependencies; use Zeek plus Wireshark if direct import is unavailable.
